First Appeal No. 541 of 1991. (Dhaka)
And
First Appeal No. 11 of 1982. (Rangpur)
lawyer:
Mr. Khondaker A.M. Mohsenuddin, Advocate ------For the appellant. 
No one ------ For the Respondent.
parties:
Agrani Bank, Nilphamari Branch ------ Appellant.
Vs.
M/S. Johan Keller and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
D.M. Ansar Uddin Ahmed, J.: This appeal at the instance of the Plaintiff is directed against the judgment and decree passed on 6.1.82 in Money Suit No. 15 of 1980 by Mr. A.K. Biswas, Subordinate Judge, Rangpur. 

 7. On 6.1.82. the suit was taken up and the learned Judge, after recording the statements of Md. Mohiuddin, passed the impugned Judgment and Decree as below:- 

 Hence, it is ordered that the suit be decreed on contest with cost. The prayer for payment of the decretal amount on yearly basis is allowed. The Jdr. to pay a sum of Tk. 6000/00 at a yearly installment. If the Jdr. fails to pay the instalment, then plaintiff do get the entire amount by starting fresh execution case. The attached property is hereby released from attachment. This installment shall run from this month." 

 8. In the decree drawn up on 13.1.82, the cost on the Plaintiff's has been assessed at Taka 4958/-. On 26.1.82, the amount of first installment was deposited, and there has been no further deposit. 

 9. It is against this Judgment and Decree that the Plaintiff has preferred the instant appeal on various grounds. There has been no appearance on behalf of any of the three Respondents to contest the appeal. It may, however, be mentioned that the notices appear to have been served upon Respondent Nos. 1 and 2, but that attempts were unsuccessfully made twice to serve upon Respondent Defendant No. 3 with the reports that there was no existence of such a firm at the stated address and ultimately process was served in the manner as provided under Order 5, Rule 20 C.P.C. 

 10. It has been urged by Mr. Khondaker A.M. Mohsen Uddin, the learned Advocate for the appellant that the learned Subordinate Judge has decreed the suit against a fictitious person inspite of serious objections raised by the Plaintiff. He submits that the learned Judge has erred in law in adding Defendant No. 3 by exercising his discretion in a most arbitrary manner and that the decree ought to have been passed against Defendants Nos. 1 and 2 with pendcntelite interest. It may be mentioned that the learned Advocate has refrained from arguing on the point of installments because of the default in deposit rendering the entire decretal dues at once recoverable. 

 11. It appears from the three petitions filed on 5.1.82 that the Petitioner was mysteriously silent as to when, from whom, under what terms or in what manner he, purchased the business' of Defendant No. 1 and as a matter of fact, no purchase document appears to have been filed in support of the prayer. The learned Judge appears to have allowed the Petitioner under Order 1, Rule 10 instantly without properly satisfying himself or giving the Plaintiff an opportunity to ascertain as to the identity and locus standi of the Petitioner. The contention that the Petitioner (Deft. No. 3) is a fictitious person has ultimately been proved true. Further, in order that a person may be added as a party, he should have a direct interest in the subject of the litigation. It is now well settled that the Court as a rule, does not add a person as a Defendant when the Plaintiff is opposed to such addition except in exceptional circumstances where the addition is absolutely necessary to adjudicate effectively and completely the matter in controversy. On the materials on record, it was quite possible to pass an effective decree in absence of the Petitioner. In our view, the learned judge has in allowing the prayer, exercised his discretion in an arbitrary and unreasonable manner. The order adding the Defendant No. 3 is, therefore, not sustainable in law. 

 12. We have quoted earlier the Judgment passed in decreeing the suit on contest against all the Defendants. It needs no mention, however, that this is palpably wrong. If at all, the suit could be decreed on admission against Defendant No. 3 only. As against the other two Defendants, the suit could not be so decreed or in absence of evidence decreed exparte, and more so because Defendant No. 1 was not duly summoned. It is clear that the suit could not be decreed in the manner as has been done. We are satisfied that the learned Judge has, passed the decree without applying his judicial mind. The entire approach has been unjudicial and the Judgment cannot be supported by any consideration of justice or under any provision of law. 

 In view of what has been stated above, we cannot find our way not to agree with Mr. Mohsenuddin that the Judgment and decree have been bad both in law as well as on facts, and as such the same are liable to be set aside. The order passed by the Court below on 5.1.82 allowing the prayer of Defendant No. 3 under Order 1, rule 10 of the code of Civil Procedures set aside and his name shall be struck off the plaint as well as the register. 

 13. The appeal is accordingly allowed without any order as to costs. The impugned Judgment and decree passed on 6.1.82 and 13.1.82 respectively by the Subordinate Judge, Rangpur, in Money Suit No. 15 of 1980 be set aside and the learned Judge is directed to proceed with the suit afresh in accordance with law after proper service of processes upon Defendants.
